links.outcome: Accuracy of LLMs versus simpler domain-specific classifier and ensembles on same test data
links.effect: SVM classifier 91.9% accuracy vs base LLM 58.7% and fine-tuned LLM 88.6%; ensembles reached 93.9% and 93.8%, outperforming either constituent (P<.001).
links.quote: The domain-specific classifier achieved 91.9% accuracy (95% CI 91.4%-92.4%), exceeding the base (58.7%) and fine-tuned (88.6%) large language models.

links.outcome: Miss rate for suicidal ideation category across models
links.effect: Base LLM missed 32.5% (650/2000) of suicidal ideation posts; hybrid ensemble missed 1.9% (37/2000), but advantage over classifier alone was not significant (P=.68).
links.quote: The hybrid ensemble reduced the miss rate for the suicidal ideation category from 32.5% (650/2000) to 1.9% (37/2000), a 17.6-fold reduction relative to the base model, although its advantage over the classifier alone within that category was not significant (P=.68).

unlisted_practices: Ensembling a domain-specific classifier with a fine-tuned LLM using closed-form bounds on LLM weighting for safety-critical classification

screen.reason: The paper focuses on developing and benchmarking ensemble architectures (combining fine-tuned LLMs with domain-specific NLP/SVM classifiers) for mental health text classification on social media data; it does not evaluate organizational deployment practices or operational safeguards.
